title: A Minnesota dam built in 1910 to generate electricity survived decades of floods
summary_full: The Rapidan Dam, an engineering marvel established more than a century ago for hydroelectric generation, is facing substantial damage from frequent flooding. The devastating floods of 2024 have rendered the structure unsafe, prompting Blue Earth County to secure significant FEMA funding for remediation. Efforts are now focused on removing the dam and restoring the badly impacted riverbanks, with demolition anticipated to start in 2027, subject to obtaining necessary permits.
